III. Overview 06

What is the Copilot SDK.

A multi-platform SDK for integrating GitHub Copilot's agentic workflows into your applications and services. No need to build your own orchestration — you define agent behavior, Copilot handles the rest.

Agentic runtime

Same production-tested engine behind Copilot CLI — planning, tool invocation, and file edits

Programmable

Full control via code — define tools, hooks, agents, and system messages programmatically

Multi-model

Access all models available via Copilot CLI — GPT, Claude, Gemini, and more

Public preview · MIT License · github.com/github/copilot-sdk

IV. Architecture 07

How it works.

All SDKs communicate with the Copilot CLI server via JSON-RPC. The SDK manages the CLI process lifecycle automatically — or connect to an external server.

🏗️
Your Application
→
📦
SDK Client
→ JSON-RPC →
⚙️
Copilot CLI
(server mode)
→
🤖
LLM Models

Bundled CLI (default)

For Node.js, Python, and .NET — CLI is bundled automatically as a dependency. No separate install needed.

External server

Run CLI in headless server mode (copilot --headless --port 4321). Multiple SDK clients can share one server.

Go and Rust: install CLI manually or opt into application-level bundling

VI. Getting started 09

First message.

Build a Copilot-powered app in about 5 lines of code. Install the SDK, create a client, send a prompt.

# main.py — Your first Copilot SDK app
from github_copilot_sdk import CopilotClient

client = CopilotClient()
session = client.create_session(model="gpt-4.1")

response = session.send_and_wait(
  prompt="What is 2 + 2?"
)
print(response.data.content)

client.stop()

Prerequisites

Copilot CLI installed and authenticated. Python 3.11+, Node.js 20+, Go 1.24+, or .NET 8.0+

Verify

Run copilot --version to confirm CLI is working. Then python main.py to run your app.

VII. Streaming 10

Streaming events.

Subscribe to 40+ real-time session events. Stream responses as they're generated for interactive UIs.

session = client.create_session(
  model="gpt-4.1",
  streaming=True,
)

# Listen for response chunks
def on_delta(event):
  print(event.data.delta_content, end="")

def on_idle(event):
  print() # Done

session.on("assistant.message_delta", on_delta)
session.on("session.idle", on_idle)

on(handler)

Subscribe to all events; returns unsubscribe function

on(eventType, handler)

Subscribe to a specific event type for targeted handling

40+ event types

Message deltas, tool calls, session lifecycle, errors, and more

VIII. Tools 11

Custom tools.

Give Copilot the ability to call your code. Define what it does, what parameters it needs, and what code to run — Copilot decides when to invoke it.

from github_copilot_sdk import define_tool

@define_tool(
  name="get_weather",
  description="Get current weather for a city",
  parameters={
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "city": {"type": "string"}
    },
  },
)
def get_weather(city: str):
  return {"city": city, "temp": "62°F"}

How it works

1. Copilot sends tool call request → 2. SDK runs your handler → 3. Result sent back → 4. Copilot uses it in response

Built-in tools

SDK also exposes Copilot CLI's first-party tools by default. Customize availability per session.

IX. Features · Hooks 12

Session hooks.

Intercept and customize session behavior at every stage. Approve or deny tool calls, transform results, filter user input, and handle errors.

Pre-tool use

Approve, deny, or modify tool calls before execution — enforce policies and guardrails

Post-tool use

Transform tool results before they reach the model — redact, enrich, or format data

User prompt

Modify or filter user messages before they're sent — add context, enforce rules

Session lifecycle

Hook into session start and end events for setup and cleanup

Pre-MCP tool call

Intercept MCP server tool calls specifically — latest hook added May 2026

Error handling

Custom error recovery logic — retry, fallback, or gracefully degrade

X. Features · Agents 13

Custom agents.

Define specialized AI personas for specific tasks — each with its own scoped tools, instructions, and behavior.

session = client.create_session(
  custom_agents=[{
    "name": "pr-reviewer",
    "display_name": "PR Reviewer",
    "description": "Reviews PRs for best practices",
    "prompt": "You are an expert code reviewer.
      Focus on security, performance, and
      maintainability.",
  }],
  agent="pr-reviewer", # pre-select
)

Scoped tools

Each agent can have its own set of tools — restrict or expand capabilities per persona.

Specialized prompts

Define persona-specific system prompts that focus the model on the right domain.

XI. Features · MCP 14

MCP integration.

Connect to Model Context Protocol servers to give your agents access to external tools and data — databases, APIs, GitHub, and more.

# Connect to GitHub's remote MCP server
session = client.create_session(
  mcp_servers={
    "github": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/",
    },
  },
)

Local & remote servers

Connect to local MCP servers via stdio or remote servers via HTTP. Mix and match per session.

GitHub MCP server

Built-in access to repos, issues, PRs, code search, and Copilot cloud agent via the GitHub MCP server.

Explore servers: github.com/mcp · modelcontextprotocol.io

XII. Features · More 15

More capabilities.

Skills

Load reusable prompt modules from directories — share expertise across agents and sessions.

Image input

Send images as attachments to sessions — enable vision-capable interactions with multimodal models.

System message control

Override, append, prepend, or remove individual system prompt sections. 10 section IDs available.

Session persistence

Resume sessions across restarts. Save and restore conversation state for long-running workflows.

Remote sessions

Share sessions to GitHub web and mobile via Mission Control — continue from any device.

Steering & queueing

Control message delivery — immediate steering vs. sequential queueing for complex workflows.

XIII. Authentication 16

Authentication methods.

Multiple ways to authenticate — from simple CLI login to enterprise OAuth flows and bring-your-own-key.

GitHub signed-in user

Uses stored OAuth credentials from copilot CLI login. Simplest option for development.

OAuth GitHub App

Pass user tokens from your GitHub OAuth app for multi-tenant SaaS applications.

Environment variables

Set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, or GITHUB_TOKEN for CI/CD and server environments.

BYOK — Bring Your Own Key

Use your own API keys from OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, Anthropic. No GitHub auth required.

Source: github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/auth/index.md

XIV. Auth · BYOK 17

Bring your own key.

Use the Copilot SDK with your own API keys from supported LLM providers — no GitHub authentication required. Key-based auth only.

OpenAI

Use your own OpenAI API key for direct access to GPT models

Azure AI Foundry

Enterprise Azure deployments with managed identity support

Anthropic

Connect directly to Anthropic's API for Claude models

Billing: With GitHub auth, each prompt counts toward your premium request quota (same as Copilot CLI). With BYOK, billing is through your LLM provider directly. A Copilot free tier is available with limited usage.

Source: github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/auth/byok.md

XV. Customization 18

System message control.

Fine-grained control over the AI's behavior. Override individual sections of the system prompt while preserving the rest.

session = client.create_session(
  system_message={
    "mode": "customize",
    "sections": {
      "tone": {
        "action": "replace",
        "content": "Be warm and professional."
      },
      "code_change_rules": {"action": "remove"},
      "guidelines": {
        "action": "append",
        "content": "Always cite sources"
      },
    },
  },
)

Section IDs: identity · tone · tool_efficiency · environment_context · code_change_rules · guidelines · safety · tool_instructions · custom_instructions · last_instructions

Actions: replace · remove · append · prepend

XVI. Production 19

Observability & deployment.

Built-in OpenTelemetry support with automatic W3C Trace Context propagation between SDK and CLI.

OpenTelemetry tracing

Export traces to OTLP endpoints or local JSON files. Automatic trace context propagation between SDK → CLI → tools.

Backend services

Run headless CLI over TCP for server-side deployments. Multiple SDK clients can share one CLI server.

Scaling & multi-tenancy

Horizontal scaling patterns, isolation per tenant, and session management for production workloads.

MAF integration

Integrate with Microsoft Agent Framework for multi-agent orchestration workflows.

Source: github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/observability/opentelemetry.md
